'''Neville Coleman''' [[Order of Australia#Appointment#Medal of the Order of Australia|OAM]] (1938 - 4 May 2012) was an Australian [[Natural history|naturalist]], underwater nature [[photographer]], writer, publisher and educator.

Coleman started [[scuba diving]] in 1963, exploring [[Port Jackson|Sydney Harbour]]. Later he joined a scientific study group and, in 1969, commenced a project aiming to document the entire [[Marine biology|marine life]] of Australia, using [[underwater photography]].

His first book, ''Australian marine fishes in colour'', was published in 1974 and he subsequently authored more than 50 books. His books included various texts for scuba divers, shell collectors, amateur naturalists and children, and typically took the forms of field guides, encyclopedias and dive guides. Departures included a collaboration with a poet and CD-ROM companions to printed publications, which included video clips of marine species. His photographs often appeared in publications by other authors on marine subjects.

In 2007 Coleman was inducted to the [[International Scuba Diving Hall of Fame]] and, in 2011, he was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) for "service to conservation and the environment through the photographic documentation of Australian marine species".<ref>{{cite web|title=Coleman, Neville Albert|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1143599|publisher=Awards and Culture Branch Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, The Australian Government|access-date=18 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120403043751/http://www.itsanhonour.gov.au/honours/honour_roll/search.cfm?aus_award_id=1143599&search_type=quick&showInd=true|archive-date=3 April 2012|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Obit">{{cite web|url=http://www.divephotoguide.com/underwater-photography-scuba-ocean-news/neville-coleman-peacefully-passes-away/ |title=Neville Coleman OAM Peacefully Passes Away -Underwater Photography Loses A Legend |publisher=Divephotoguide.com |date=2012-05-04 |access-date=2012-10-10}}</ref> Coleman died of natural causes at 4:55{{nbsp}}am on 4 May 2012, in his sleep.<ref name="Obit"/>

== Taxon named in his honor ==
Coleman discovered many marine creatures new to science. Several species of [[fish]], [[Nudibranchia|nudibranchs]] and other [[invertebrate]]s have been named after him, including:
*The [[Mantis shrimps|mantis shrimp]] ''[[Lysiosquilla colemani]]''
*The nudibranch ''[[Chromodoris colemani]]''
*The pygmy [[seahorse]] ''[[Hippocampus colemani]]''
*Coleman's melibe or ghost melibe ''[[Melibe colemani]]''
*The Sand perch ''[[Parapercis colemani]]''<ref name = ETYFish>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/uranoscopiformes/ | title = Order Uranoscopiformes: Pinguipedidae, Cheimarrichthyidae, Ammodytidae and Uranoscopidae | access-date = 6 March 2022 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | name-list-style = amp | work = The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | date = 22 September 2018 | archive-date = 6 March 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220306084648/http://etyfish.org/uranoscopiformes/ | url-status = dead }}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Neville Coleman Memorial Dives are held annually,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Baker|first=Janine|title=The Neville Coleman Memorial Nudibranch Dive. Summary of Results from Community Dive Events in South Australia in 2015 and 2016|url=https://www.academia.edu/27889498|language=en}}</ref> with special events including a [[sea slug]] photo competition and public art exhibition held in South Australia.
